sentiment.instructions: Decide whether the tweet carries an explicit positive or negative stance, through feeling words, emoticons, eager hype, the author's own praise or put-down, or a clearly good or bad event. If there is no such signal, choose neutral, even if the author talks about themselves. Exclamation marks alone are not a signal.

criteria.positive: Positive feeling or praise: love, like, fun, best, perfect, brilliant, impressed, amazing, cool, hope, pray, blessings, celebrate, can't wait, let's go, wow, :). Includes hedged praise of the author's own experience, confident praise or defense of someone, and the author's eager anticipation of their own concert, show or outing. Also eager promotions (check it out, come support, please share, get your tickets now, win), condolences that bless someone, and completed successes such as titles, finals reached, records or historic firsts.
criteria.neutral: No stance signal. Covers flat plans, event notices, ticket sales, spam, requests even with a thanks or <3, scores and in-progress game updates, trivia, questions and speculation. Also headlines that report criticism or controversy about companies or politicians (worst offense, bad reputation, apology, correction), wry snark about an athlete's performance or stats, mockery softened by laughter (haha, bwahaha, lol), comic hyperbole about oneself, matter-of-fact mishaps or apologies (computer broke, sorry for the delay), and hedged comparisons about public figures.
criteria.negative: Negative feeling: sad, hate, annoyed, ugh, ACK, wtf, damn, bad mood, can't sleep, going to die, miss, sucks, disappointed, :(. Also the author's own put-downs: belittling comparisons, mocking remarks about someone's looks or fans, sarcastic labels, cynical rhetorical questions about politicians, complaints, insults, and hostile political or religious arguments. Also news of real harm even if worded flatly: deaths, attacks, missile strikes, riots, bombings, crimes, charges, scandals, injuries, deficits and product failures.
